sources_considered.why: The original GPT-4 technical report documents reliability limitations before the post.
The incident record also reports restored normal operation, an important limit on interpreting an incident as permanent instability.
Documents both useful operation and conversational failures, but supplies no longitudinal stability threshold.
Examines stability under different prompts on a narrow medical examination task; it does not measure sustained ordinary operation. The extracted conclusion also interleaves reference text.
Tests tracking of synthetic environment states, which does not settle the broader historical claim.

evidence_items.explanation: The report establishes acknowledged reliability problems in GPT-4 before the incident. Imperfect reliability in one model does not establish that generative AI systems have never been stable.

evidence_items.locator: Resolved update, displayed as February 20, 2024, 11:14 PM
evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI reported restoration of normal operation. This weighs against treating the episode as uninterrupted malfunction, but a recovery announcement is not a longitudinal demonstration of stability.

unresolved_gaps: No source examined establishes the class-wide historical assertion under an ordinary reliability standard.
The claim specifies no duration, workload, or acceptable failure rate that would distinguish stable operation from imperfect operation.
Incident records and narrow task evaluations do not establish either perpetual instability or sustained general reliability.
